summary: Fetch builds the request, returns an error naming the code on non-200 responses, and decodes the rate, so both criteria hold. However, resp.Body is never closed on any path (success, non-200, or decode error). Every call leaks the connection and its file descriptor and stops keep-alive reuse. Under checkout traffic this exhausts sockets. The test covers only the 200 path.

findings.title: Response body is never closed, leaking connections on every Fetch
findings.detail: After c.HTTP.Do succeeds, Fetch returns on the non-200 branch, the decode-error branch, and the success branch without calling resp.Body.Close(). net/http requires callers to close the body. Otherwise the underlying TCP connection is neither returned to the pool nor released, so each checkout conversion leaks a connection and goroutines. Under load this ends in file-descriptor exhaustion and failing rate lookups.
findings.fix: Right after the error check, add `defer resp.Body.Close()`. Optionally drain the body with io.Copy(io.Discard, resp.Body) before closing on the non-200 path so the connection can be reused.

findings.title: No test for the non-200 path in criterion 2
findings.detail: TestFetch only serves a 200 with {"rate":1.08}. No test has the server answer 404 for XXX and assert an error that contains "XXX".
findings.fix: Add a case where the handler calls http.NotFound for /rates/XXX, and assert that Fetch returns a non-nil error whose message contains "XXX".

criteria.evidence: Fetch decodes {"rate":1.08} and returns body.Rate; TestFetch asserts 1.08 for EUR; evidence/criterion-1.jsonl.
For a non-200 status, Fetch returns fmt.Errorf("rates: %s: %s", code, resp.Status), which names XXX; evidence/criterion-2.jsonl. No unit test covers this path.
